The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f1e921ab8ebfe061baec70b6113dee12b6360b4f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

git fetch origin ae7ef0e906bd74c4acd17d618d511739c2168921 && git checkout ae7ef0e906bd74c4acd17d618d511739c2168921

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept set: nothing moves — right.** The diff changes one template literal's tail inside the `REACT_PROP_DEPRECATED` push at `packages/lint/src/validate-react-page-props.ts:1198`. The condition that reaches it (`block.deprecated.get(u)`), the rule id, the `warning` severity, `where`, `path` and `hint: dep.note` are untouched, and the prefix `TAG prop "PROP" is the deprecated spelling of the metadata-tier "REPLACED_BY"` (TAG, PROP and REPLACED_BY standing for the `tag`, `u` and `dep.replacedBy` interpolations, which are byte-identical) is the same on both sides. Only ` and is removed after the deprecation window (#11284).` becomes `: the react tier converges on the metadata-tier vocabulary, so this spelling keeps working through the deprecation window and is removed after it.` Same findings, same shape, new words.

**The words are true to the decision's surviving record — right.** #11284 answers 404 (the dev's measurement, with #5583 as the 200 control; not re-probed here). The record that stands is the `@objectstack/lint` CHANGELOG entry `5383fa6` (maintainer ruling 2026-08-23: the react tier converges on the metadata-tier spelling, deprecate-first; the deprecated aliases stay published and accepted for the whole deprecation window, every use warns and never errors, removal comes after the window), and commit `5383fa670`'s own diff is where this exact message line was written, together with the `REACT_PROP_DEPRECATED` docblock and the `ReactInteractionProp.deprecated` docblock in `packages/spec/src/ui/react-blocks.ts`, both of which still state that contract at this head. The new sentence says that decision and adds nothing. The one clause the record later reversed (the ListView aliases went with no window, #14791) belongs to the `retired` path and its own rule and message; this message describes the `deprecated` mechanism, whose "removed after" clause the old text already carried. Form D as ruling C+D states it: the lesson in words, no number to look up. The gate's own id regex (`INTERNAL_ID_SOURCE`: a hash followed by 3 to 5 digits, not preceded by a hash or ampersand) matched `11284` in the old text and matches nothing in the new.

**The prose-id ratchet moves in its allowed direction — right.** The gate's header rules: growth (measured above pinned) reds; shrink (measured below pinned) reds as STALE with the remedy "regenerate the baseline in this same PR", and "shrink is the landing author's to take, growth is not". This diff is that remedy. `scripts/doc-authoring-prose-id.baseline.json` loses the one line `"#11284": 1` under `packages/lint/src/validate-react-page-props.ts`, keeps `"#5583": 1` there, and nothing else moves: 230 files on both sides, 621 (file, id) pairs before and 620 after, 948 pinned occurrences before and 947 after (the dev's 810 / 809 is the gate's own count of id-bearing string sites, one per string; not re-run here, and the JSON diff is exactly that one pair either way). The file parses as JSON at the head. Equality with the gate's ledger, read from the code: this leg counts ids in non-comment, non-test string literals under `packages/` minus `packages/spec`; in the one file this diff touches, every hash-number at the head sits in a `//` or `*` comment except `objectstack#5583` at `:458`, one string, so the measured entry is `#5583: 1`, equal to the head's baseline entry; no other file moved, and the 4 commits `main` gained since the base (`f1e921ab8e`, `04b202e5cb`, `5363e2dc64`, `4d04b6be30`) touch neither this file nor the baseline nor the changeset (`git log` over the three paths is empty). The CI job that runs `pnpm check:doc-authoring` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `lint.yml:2145`) is the authority for the measured equality and had not concluded at my read (③).

**Pins: none — confirmed by grep.** At the head, `git grep` for `removed after the deprecation window` and `deprecation window (#11284)` finds nothing; `deprecated spelling of the metadata-tier` finds only `:1198`. `REACT_PROP_DEPRECATED` / `react-prop-deprecated` appears in the source, the `index.ts` barrel, `validate-react-page-props.test.ts` (rule-id assertions only: the `pastDeprecation` filter at `:37` and `toEqual([])` at `:116` and `:204`; every `message` assertion in that file is on another rule), two release-owned CHANGELOGs and this PR's changeset. No pin to flip, and none owed: wording is not pinned unless a consumer parses it.

The baseline is a repo-internal gate ledger. The generated react-blocks contract and `skills/objectstack-ui/references/react-blocks.md` carry the contract's `note` and `description`, not the lint message, so nothing is owed there.

**The rule is dormant today — true, from source.** `REACT_BLOCKS` in `packages/spec/src/ui/react-blocks.ts` (4 tags: ObjectForm, ListView, ObjectChart, Block) declares `deprecated` on no interaction; the lint builds each block's `deprecated` map from exactly that field, so every map is empty and the branch at `:1193` cannot run. The only spellings ever deprecated, ListView `objectName` / `viewType`, sit in `REACT_RETIRED_OVERLAY_PROPS` and report `react-prop-retired`. It does not change this diff: the mechanism and its message stay for the next deprecation, and the text an author would then read is the one judged above.
